# Reports, one page of lenses: design spec

**Date:** 2 Oct 2026 · **Owner:** Ruben · **Status:** design approved in brainstorming (canvas R1-R9 and the data
catalog, 2 Oct: "all will be approved as you best suggest"); this spec awaits Ruben's review · **Plans:** one per phase
(§5), written after this spec is approved.
**Canvas:** `Downloads/reports-liquid-glass.html`, generated by `Claude Video/docs/reports-canvas/reports_canvas.py`
(outside the repo). **Data catalog:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-reports-lenses-data-catalog.md` (every field,
event and gap per lens, with `file:line`). **Builds on:** `2026-09-18-reports-redesign-design.md` (the chart kit, the
palette, Worth knowing and the Ask door stay; its single-page layout is replaced), decision 0015 (Reports is the
shell's pilot surface), the interface kit PRD `docs/plans/2026-09-28-the-interface-kit-and-its-looks.md`.

Written against origin/main `32328415f`. Paths are from the repo root unless they start with `dashboard/`, which is
`apps/dashboard/src/`.

## 1. Goal

Reports becomes one page with a **lens per thing the business runs**, each at its own address, so an owner reads how the
period went in one sentence and goes one tap deeper only where they care:

1. **Overview**: how did the period go, and what needs a look?
2. **Receptionist**: is it handling my customers, and how fast against the hold I set?
3. **People**: who are they, are they growing, can I reach them, are they coming back?
4. **Calendar**: are my hours filling?
5. **Pipeline** (proposal businesses): what becomes a client, how fast, and why not?
6. **Campaigns**: what went out, who it reached, and what came back?
7. **Reviews**: what do customers say in public?
8. **Usage** (owner): how much of my plan have I used, and what did it do?
9. **Leads** (finder workspaces): is the finder paying for itself?

Second goal: the backend starts keeping what the lenses need and does not keep today, in an order where every capture
lands before the tile that reads it, because data not kept today can never be reported later.

## 3. Decisions taken in brainstorming

| # | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | One page, lenses as sub-addresses `/w/<slug>/reports/<lens>`; `/reports` is the Overview. | One reader per number, matches the sidebar's nouns, keeps the page's mount (People's pattern). |
| D2 | Lenses: Overview, Receptionist, People, Calendar, Pipeline, Campaigns, Reviews, Usage, Leads. Team later. The operator fleet is a separate back-office report on the same metric registry. | The canvas; the catalog. |
| D3 | A lens shows only once its thing has happened (§6.2). | A salon that books never sees Pipeline; nobody sees an empty Leads. |
| D4 | The head stays **Reports** on every lens; the lens's headline is the head's standing sentence; the strip says which lens. | Switching lenses never moves the head; the sentence is the lens's answer. |
| D5 | The strip is a row of **links** (a view that changes the address is a link: the kit's rule). SubTabs gains an `href` variant; on a phone the strip scrolls sideways with the chosen lens centred. | Kit rule; addresses are shareable and Ask can cite them. |
| D6 | Each lens owns its period: presets 7 / 30 / 90 days and Month (calendar days in the workspace's time zone, against the same length before); Usage uses billing periods (a Select); no custom range in this program. | Today's API refuses other days; a range picker is a kit variant later. |
| D7 | Every lens has the same five parts: its sentence; what came in against the period before; the funnel or the mix; the time between steps; what is stuck now, as doors into the work page. | The reader always knows where to look. |
| D8 | Reports count what changed; a stock is drawn only "as of now" and as a door into its work page, never as a second list. | One home per fact. |
| D9 | A number with no source is **absent, never zero**; a ratio shows its count (n) and greys under a minimum. | Nothing the database can't say; small samples mislead. |
| D10 | Change words are plain ink. Amber is only what needs you, red only what failed, coral only the selected and the live. | The kit's badge rules. |
| D11 | **Usage speaks in the plan's share, never minutes or dollars**; money stays on Billing; list-price model dollars belong to the operator. | Ruben's 25 Sep usage direction; dollars are Chanlytics' costs, not the owner's. |
| D12 | **Worth, never revenue**, until payments write deals (decision 0005). | Amounts are what proposals say. |
| D13 | No single "AI accuracy" score. The Overview says two numbers: how much the receptionist took, and how much of that it settled. | Verifiable events, not a graded score. |
| D14 | Reply speed is measured **against the reply hold** the owner set, apart from the receptionist's own time. | Today's number mostly measures the setting. |
| D15 | Automated sends (playbooks, broadcasts, reach-outs) never count as "you". | The audit's #4. |
| D16 | Out-of-hours reads the workspace's own hours. | Today's 8-to-8 says 22 where the salon's hours say 33. |
| D17 | Overview and Today read one small **headline read**, never the whole page. | Today's boot pays for the heaviest read in the product. |
| D18 | One **metric registry**: an id, its words, its definition, its window, its source and who may see it; every figure on every lens carries an id. | Three definitions of "new person" exist today. |
| D19 | No open rates, no email click tracking (decision 8), no sentiment or "time saved" headline, no leaderboard, no retention for windows that haven't matured. | The benchmark's avoid list; earlier decisions. |
| D20 | The dashed tags on the canvas are notes, not product. | They mark what needs wiring. |

## 4. Principles the page holds

1. Every figure says what it counts in words an owner uses, and its definition is one hover or long-press away (Tooltip from the registry).
2. One sentence per tile, adding the next thing; never a paragraph.
3. A tile is a door: its figure or its row opens the work page filtered to exactly those people or conversations.
4. Charts follow the kit and the dataviz rules: thin marks, a legend whenever there are two or more series, one scale per chart (never two axes), a table view and a CSV on every chart card.
5. Phone first: work before chrome. The phone shows the strip and one period capsule, then the tiles; detail opens as the kit's Sheet.

## 5. The program: six phases, each its own plan

Each phase is a plan of its own (`docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-reports-<phase>.md`, dated the day it is written), written when it starts.
Nothing is pushed until Ruben says so; each phase is verified on the local app first.

| Phase | What | Depends on | Visible? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Fix today's page** | The four wrong numbers and the vocabulary (§12). | nothing | yes, small |
| **B. The frame** | Addresses, the lens registry, the head, the strip, periods, the headline read (Today switches), today's sections moved into their lenses unchanged, the metric registry, Figure and the other kit parts B needs. | `kit/phone-threads` landed (SubTabs, Menu sheet, `warmRoute`); #1367 (one look) merged | yes |
| **C. Draw what's stored** | One PR per lens adding every tile the catalog marks **Now**; Calendar and Leads lenses. | B | yes |
| **D. Start keeping** | The **Small** captures (§10), each its own PR, each before the tile that reads it. | none (can run beside B and C) | no, until its tile |
| **E. The appointments record** | Decision 0002 built, plus the feed keeping status and created times; then the tiles that need it. Its own spec. | K3 (first touch) for attribution | yes |
| **F. Outputs and fleet** | The weekly email, ranges past 90 days, the operator fleet report (own spec), a share link last. | B; K10 for long ranges | yes |

Order: A first (small, independent). B next. D runs beside B and C, lowest-numbered first. C lens by lens. E after K3. F last.

## 6. The frame (phase B)

### 6.1 Addresses

- `apps/dashboard/app/(os)/w/[workspace]/reports/page.tsx` becomes `reports/[[...lens]]/page.tsx`.
- The route row (`dashboard/surfaces/routes.ts:78`) gains `takes: (p) => isLensId(p)`, `mount: "reports"` (the page stays mounted across lenses; a lens move is patched history, `onOnePage`) and `chrome: reportsChrome` (the crumbs: Reports, and the lens where it is not the Overview).
- Lens ids are the address words: `receptionist`, `people`, `calendar`, `pipeline`, `campaigns`, `reviews`, `usage`, `leads`. `/reports/overview` is not an address; the Overview is `/reports`.
- A lens id that exists but is not shown for this workspace draws that lens's empty state ("Leads appear once you search for businesses", a door to where that starts), never a not-found: Ask and ⌘K may link it.
- The period is not in the address in this program; it is kept per lens in `localStorage` (`chanlytics.report.period.<lens>`), as today's single period is.

### 6.2 The lens registry and who sees what

`packages/contracts/src/reports/lenses.ts`: one table, read by the strip, the route row, ⌘K, Ask and the headline read.

| Lens | Shown when | Default period | Periods | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Overview | always | 30 days | 7 / 30 / 90 / Month | member |
| Receptionist | always | 30 days | 7 / 30 / 90 / Month | member |
| People | always | 30 days | 7 / 30 / 90 / Month | member |
| Calendar | a calendar feed is connected | 30 days (booked hours: this week and next) | 7 / 30 / 90 | member |
| Pipeline | `tenants.sells_by = 'proposal'` and a deal was ever recorded | 90 days | 30 / 90 / Month | member |
| Campaigns | a playbook, broadcast or reach-out ever sent | 30 days | 7 / 30 / 90 / Month | member |
| Reviews | always; with no listing linked it draws its empty state, the door to Find it | 30 days | 7 / 30 / 90 / Month | member |
| Usage | always, for the owner | this billing period | billing periods | owner |
| Leads | a lead search ever ran | 30 days | 7 / 30 / 90 | member |

"Shown when" is computed once per boot by the headline read (`has` per lens), so the strip never flickers.

### 6.3 The head, the strip and the period

- The page calls `useStanding({ title: "Reports", sentence: <the lens's headline> })` (`dashboard/surfaces/kit/head/standing.ts:64`). On a phone the head shows the name only (the Glass phone rule) and the sentence is the first line of the first tile.
- The strip is `SubTabs` with an `href` per tab (new variant, §8), drawn as links with the sliding lozenge; a pointer on a tab warms that lens (`warmRoute` for the address, and the lens's read through the surface's held views).
- The period is the kit's `Segmented` (7 days, 30 days, 90 days, Month); Usage's is a `Select` of billing periods. On a phone both fold into one capsule (`Select`) beside the strip.
- The row's right end: "Ask about this lens" and a `Menu` (Export this lens as CSV, Print, the weekly email).

### 6.4 One read per lens

For each lens, as it is built (7 Oct 2026; Reviews, the first lens of phase C, is the one that fits all of it, and Campaigns has its function and its reader but is still read through the frame; the Receptionist lens, C2, fits it too since 10 Oct 2026):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQL | A function for the lens's own read, in a migration named for what it adds: `report_series` (00304, the Overview, Receptionist and People lenses), `campaign_series` (00329), `reviews_ledger(p_tenant_id, p_days)` (00350), `receptionist_series(p_tenant_id, p_days, p_end)` (00380, the Receptionist lens's own read: what `report_series` does not hold, over the window and, for the parts set against before, the one before it) | SECURITY INVOKER, so the caller's RLS decides; one statement, so one snapshot; the window said once, in the tenant's own time zone (`p_days` is the days of the period, which the route works out: Month is the days since the 1st); capped at 90 days of daily rows until the rollup (K10); 00251 is the pattern. Called from a `packages/db` repository function (`packages/db/src/repositories/reports/report-series.ts`), never by name from the dashboard. |
| Route | `GET /api/v1/reports/<lens>?period=` | `read({ scope: workspace, rate: "aggregate" })`; the period parsed by one shared zod schema (`ReportQuery`); a row in `tooling/scripts/tests/route-policy.json`, the typed client regenerated (`route-types.mjs`), `docs/api.md` regenerated. Built: `reports` (the Receptionist lens's read, and the Overview's), `reports/campaigns`, `reports/reach-outs`, `reports/headline`, `reports/receptionist` and `reports/reviews`. `days`, which the pages sent before there was a Month, is read by no report route since 10 October 2026 (a request that still sends it is read as one that did not: thirty days); the headline's and Reviews' routes take `period` alone. |
| Reader | `dashboard/src/server/readers/report.ts` (`report`, `reportHeadline`, `reviewsReport`, `receptionistReport`) and `campaign-report.ts` | The one reader for the page and for Ask's tool; a turn reads Google once (`readers/connections.ts`). Booking and deals are still counted in TypeScript from People and the calendar: moving them into SQL is phase C's later work. |
| Contracts | `packages/contracts/src/reports/`, one folder, a module to a concern | The DTO type, `to<Lens>VM` and the sentence builders: Reviews' are `review-report.ts` (its figures and every sentence) over `review-record.ts` (its counts); the Receptionist's are `receptionist/receptionist-report.ts` (its figures and every sentence) over `receptionist/receptionist-record.ts` (the DTO, its guard and builder, which the server reads). A lens's fold and its words are a page-only entry, `@chanlytics/contracts/report-lens` (`PAGE_ONLY` in `tooling/scripts/gen/contracts-browser-entry.mjs`, with `report-window`): the browser entry every page's route loads leaves them out, so a word only Reports draws is not paid for by every page. Every sentence the page draws is in the view model. The demo sample is the surface's (`dashboard/src/surfaces/reports/sample.ts`: `reportsSample`, `reviewsSample` for Reviews and `receptionistSample` for the Receptionist), made through the real fold. Every figure carries a registry id (§7). |
| Surface | `dashboard/src/surfaces/reports/`: `surface.ts` (`reports`, read for every lens by the frame), `reviews-surface.ts` (`reports_reviews`, Reviews' own) and `receptionist-surface.ts` (`reports_receptionist`, the Receptionist's own: the DTO as the route gave it and when it was read, which the page folds), all three over `periodSurface` (`period-surface.ts`) for what a period's read needs | Held views keyed by period (`heldViews(4)`): going back to a period paints at once and reads behind. A lens with a surface of its own is read where the lens is drawn and nowhere else, and forgotten, not re-read, by a write made on another page. |
| Page | `dashboard/surfaces/reports/lenses/<lens>.tsx` | Kit parts only; the page's stylesheet holds layout alone. |

### 6.5 The headline read, and Today

- `GET /api/v1/reports/headline?period=` over `report_headline(p_tenant, p_period)`: per visible lens its `has`, one figure, its words, its change and its sentence; the Overview's own figures (handled without you, while you were closed, booked) and Worth a look's facts. Target: under 150 ms warm server time, under 6 KB.
- It is the Overview's read, and the read Today draws its period line and leaks from. `ROUTE_DRAWS.today` swaps `reports` for `reports_headline`; `card.tsx:319` and `leaks.tsx:46` read the new surface.
- Today's boot loses `report_series`, the people pool, the feed and the deals for Reports' sake. Measured on `next start` (`:3310`) before and after.

### 6.6 Live refresh

Each lens names the tables it repaints on from the workspace topic (00265; `packages/db/src/realtime.ts`), only while it is on screen (`onlyOnItsPage`), debounced 800 ms:

| Lens | Tables |
| --- | --- |
| Overview, Receptionist | messages, conversations, escalations, calls |
| People | messages, calls, segment_members |
| Pipeline | deals |
| Campaigns | messages, reach_out_replies |
| Reviews | google_reviews (a review seen for the first time), google_listings, google_connections; the daily readings and the reply events are not on the topic: read with the rest, and again after a reply posted from the page |
| Leads | leads, lead_rounds, lead_search_members, reach_out_replies |
| Calendar, Usage | none: read on visit (the feed and the ledger are not on the topic) |

### 6.7 Ask, ⌘K and citations

- Ask's report tool (`dashboard/server/ask/tools/read/report.ts`) takes a period, not yet a lens, and reads the report, the Campaigns lens's reader and the Reviews lens's, so what it says of Campaigns and Reviews is the page's (a lens's sentence and figures from the same fold); today it still misses the reach-outs.
- Each lens's view model exports at most four figures in Ask's `show.figures` shape (`packages/contracts/src/ask/ask-answer.ts:39-64`), so "Ask about this lens" and the lens show the same block.
- ⌘K lists each visible lens (`packages/contracts/src/ask/ask-jump.ts:50`); citations accept `reports/<lens>` (`citations.ts:86,103`; the prefix already takes one segment).
- The Overview's Ask tile offers three questions built from that period's facts.

### 6.8 Export and print

Every chart card keeps its Chart/Table switch and CSV (the phone app's share sheet already takes it). The lens Menu adds "Export this lens" (one CSV of every figure with its registry id and definition) and Print (the print stylesheet, per lens).

### 6.9 Phone

The strip scrolls sideways with the chosen lens centred and the period as one capsule; tiles stack; a tile's detail opens as the kit's `Sheet`, each row a door. Reports stays behind More in the phone app (no new tab).

### 6.10 Demo

Each lens has a sample, drawn in a declared demo session: `surfaces/reports/sample.ts` holds `reportsSample` (the Overview, Receptionist, People, Pipeline and Campaigns lenses) and `reviewsSample` (Reviews: the listing as Google shows it with no profile behind it, through the real fold, so the demo draws the same section a workspace does).

## 7. The metric registry

`packages/contracts/src/reports/metrics.ts`:

```ts
interface Metric {
  id: MetricId;                 // "receptionist.answered_by_ai", "people.new", ...
  lens: LensId;
  words: string;                // what the figure says under it
  definition: string;           // the tooltip: what is counted and what is not
  window: "calendar-days" | "cohort" | "as-of-now" | "billing-period";
  source: string;               // the SQL function and its field
  role: "member" | "owner";
  minN?: number;                // a ratio greys and says its count below this
}
```

- One definition per id, held by a test that every figure in every lens view model names a registry id, and every id is defined once.
- "New person" gets one rule (first spoken word or connected call; erased people excluded) in `report_series`, `metrics_summary` and `person_moments.new_at` alike.
- The fleet report and the weekly email read the same ids.

## 8. Kit additions

Each follows the kit's "Add a variant" or "Add a component" steps (`.claude/skills/chanlytics-interface/SKILL.md`): its rule in `kit.css` reading tokens, its name in `classes.json`, its gallery entry, its type test, and for Base UI parts its running-page entry and browser test.

| Part | What | Phase | Also used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Figure** (`kit/figure/`) | a number, its words, a change in plain ink, a sub-line, an optional door (`href`), an optional `n` that greys under `minN` | B | Today's figures, Pipeline, Deals |
| **SubTabs `href`** | the strip as links, keeping the sliding lozenge | B | any addressed strip (the kit's `.stabs` successor) |
| **Charts on the pane roles** | `ChartCard` draws inside `Panel` `pane`; `charts.css` reads `--surface-pane-*`; Reports' page rules for panes go | B | every chart |
| **Meter `pace`** | a tick where an even pace would be today | C | Usage, Leads |
| **Funnel** (`kit/charts/funnel.tsx`) | steps with the share moving on, an optional ghost step, an outcome split as a SegmentBar | C | Overview, Leads, Campaigns, Pipeline, Receptionist |
| **HeatGrid** | weekday x hour, with the workspace's hours as a band per row (generalises HeatStrip) | C | Receptionist, People, Calendar |
| **DotPlot** | one dot per event against a reference line | C | Receptionist (speed against the hold) |
| **Histogram with n** | a BarChart variant that shows counts and greys under `minN` | C | People, Calendar |
| **DotMap** | centroids on a plain ground, no tiles | C7 | Leads, later People |

The first Base UI part a surface draws raises the route's JS budget in that change (`check:bundle -- --raise`), argued in `docs/debt.md`.

## 11. The appointments record (phase E)

Its own spec, building decision 0002 ("decided, not built"): a row per visit from the feed sync with `status` (the parser
keeps CANCELLED instead of dropping it), the feed's created time, `service`, the price where the service has one, and
what came before it (`attributed_to`: the message, call or send). "Missed" only by a person's door; nothing is inferred
from silence. It unlocks: kept/missed/cancelled, how far ahead, booked by the receptionist, new/returning/rebooked, the
usual gap and at-risk, lifetime per client, booked after a campaign, and the Overview's "booked" made exact.
Writers: `packages/contracts/src/calendar/feed.ts:22-37,248-250`, `apps/edge/api/cron/calendar.ts:101-106`.

## 13. Testing and proof

- **Moves (B):** each section moved into its lens is equal by value (the view model for the same DTO before and after, decision 0015); CSS is proved by both style-equality recorders; `tooling/scripts/tests/reports/*` re-pointed.
- **SQL:** each `report_<lens>` has a `.db` test over fixtures in the pattern of `report-days.db`: time-zone day edges, the prior period, an erased person, an automated send, a call that never connected.
- **Contracts:** every view model builder has unit tests for its sentences, absent-not-zero, and `minN` greying; the registry test (§7).
- **Kit:** gallery entries, type tests, `kit-components` maps, `kit-behaves` for Base UI parts, `e2e/kit/*` specs.
- **Page:** `e2e/reports.spec.ts` grows per lens (the strip moves without a reload, the period sticks per lens, a hidden lens's empty state, the phone sheet); harness captures desk 1440 and phone 390 in both themes.
- **Ask:** an eval case per lens question ("how did my campaigns do this month?") reads the lens's reader.
- **Today's boot:** request count and time before and after B3, measured on `next start`.
- Tests and docs never name a real customer's workspace (use `harbor`, `acme`).
- Every PR: packages' `dist` rebuilt and committed, `route-policy.json` and the generated client and `docs/api.md` current, `docs/debt.md` rows for any ratchet raised (the bundle budget for Base UI parts), and the measures in `docs/debt.md` only falling.

## 14. Budgets (targets, measured on `next start`)

| What | Target |
| --- | --- |
| Headline read | ≤ 150 ms warm server time, ≤ 6 KB |
| A lens's read | ≤ 400 ms warm server time, ≤ 40 KB |
| Moving between lenses already read | painted in one frame from held views |
| Moving to a lens not yet read | first paint ≤ 1 s on a warm instance |
| Today's boot | no read of `report_series`, the people pool, the feed or deals for Reports |

## 15. Rollout

- Local first: every phase is verified on the local app and pushed only on Ruben's word, batched (his standing rules).
- Phase A can ship alone.
- Phase B lands with the lenses holding exactly today's sections (Overview from the headline read), so nothing an owner sees disappears; phase C then fills one lens per PR.
- `/reports` keeps working throughout: it is the Overview.
- The demo session draws each lens's sample (Reviews' too).

## 16. Out of scope, and what not to build

Out of scope: money actually paid (decision 0005); a custom date range (a DatePicker range variant later); review
requests and competitor ratings (§18); Google profile insights; the Team lens (later, counts not rankings, only with
more than one member); a share link (phase F, last); the operator fleet report (its own spec).

Not to build: a single AI accuracy or resolution score; open rates; email click tracking (decision 8); LLM sentiment,
"time saved" or ROI multiples as headlines; developer metrics (latency, concurrency, cost per call) on an owner's page;
leaderboards; retention for windows that have not matured; a ratio without its count.

## 17. Risks

| Risk | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Phase B depends on work not on main (`kit/phone-threads`, the People kit, #1367). | B starts after they land; A and D do not wait. |
| Nine SQL functions over 90 days each get slow. | One pass per source (00251's pattern), the person indexes (00253), Server-Timing on every lens read, the budgets in §14. |
| Definitions drift between lenses, Today, Ask and the email. | The registry and its test (§7). |
| The calendar feed is slow or down. | Calendar reads on visit, says "couldn't read your calendar" in its own tile, and the rest of the page stands. |
| Ask's context grows with nine lenses. | At most four figures per lens in Ask's block; the tool reads one lens at a time. |
| A real workspace's report is trusted while its intake is broken (the salon showed nothing inbound from Sep 21 to Oct 2). | A silence fact in Worth a look ("nothing new since …, the longest in 60 days") with a door to the lines; checking that workspace's intake is separate work. |

## 18. Ruben's decisions still open

1. **The plan bar's unit**: Usage's top tile waits on the pricing decision (PR #1039, numbered 0011, a number another decision has since taken).
2. **Review requests**: a playbook that asks for a review a day after a kept visit (needs phase E); then Reviews can show asked → reviewed.
3. **Link clicks on WhatsApp and SMS** (a first-party redirect): email stays without tracking either way.
4. **Competitors near you** on Reviews: reading other businesses' public listings each day.
5. **The Team lens**: when a workspace has more than one member.
